text:
maya: Heads up — cluster-autoscaler failed to scale down gpu-nodepool-3 again. CA says some pods are not evictable, but I can't see any PDBs that would block it. Any ideas?
lee: Which pods? can you paste the autoscaler event?
maya: infra-bot posted the event: 
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scale-down-blocked: node/gpu-node-45 not suitable for removal: Pod(s) on node are not evictable: inference/pi-service-rt-7b (safe-to-evict=false), checkpoint-operator-0 (local-storage)
sam: ah that explains it. We added `safe-to-evict: "false"` on the long-running RT pods to avoid mid-request eviction. But that also blocks CA.
ash: (typo: ash) We should be careful — marking pods non-evictable prevents any automated scale-down. For GPU pools we do want to allow scale down when node is idle for Xm.
lee: Options: 1) Set a short grace period and annotate pods dynamically during drain windows. 2) Use PDBs with minAvailable set to allow one replica to be killed but not all. 3) Rely on priority classes + preemption to let CA evict low-priority pods.
maya: Thinking through constraints: inference pods are stateful (cache in local tmpfs) and long-running; they do restore state after restart but take ~30s. For latency-critical requests we don't want to interrupt. But during off-peak, interruption is fine.
sam: Proposed plan: add an autoscaler-aware annotation on our Deployments and a controller that flips `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true` during maintenance windows/scale checks. That keeps usual safe-to-evict=false during normal ops.
lee: Another low-effort approach: add a PDB for the replicaSet with `minAvailable: 1` and run the deployment with at least 2 replicas in the GPU pool. Then CA can kill a node if one replica remains. Example PDB YAML:
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: inference-rt-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference-rt
```
That keeps one pod alive.
maya: But some services have single-replica jobs pinned to local GPU. PDB doesn't help there.
ash: For singletons we should use a PriorityClass to make them less important for scale-down. For example give non-critical batch jobs `priorityClassName: low-inference` and high-latency-critical `critical-inference`. CA will consider podpriority? (note: CA respects eviction constraints like safe-to-evict and PDB; preemption isn't directly used by CA to evict pods on scale-down)
sam: Right — CA won't preempt to free space. It only simulates evicting and checks if pods are evictable. So priority class alone won't help for CA decisions. We need to make pods evictable or ensure redundancy.
lee: Practical steps I recommend:
- Audit pods in GPU pools for `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict` and local-storage mounts.
- Add a lightweight controller that toggles safe-to-evict based on traffic signals and a timed scale-check window.
- Require at least 2 replicas for stateless GPU services that need high availability.
- For singleton/ephemeral jobs, prefer spot/burst pool with different lifecycle or set `scale-down-disabled` annotation on node to avoid surprise.
maya: Implementation question: how would the controller decide when to set safe-to-evict=true? CPU/GPU utilization + request rate threshold?
ash: Yes, use combined signals: GPU util < 10% for 15m and QPS < N, and no active long-lived debug sessions. When conditions match, flip annotation on pods and add a short TTL to revert.
sam: Also ensure we don't accidentally make pods evictable during live experiments. Add an override label `maintenance-allowed=true` that ops can toggle.
lee: Edge cases: CA scale-down will still respect DaemonSets and PDBs and will fail if local-storage present unless you use `--delete-local-data` with kubectl drain. CA will not force-delete local-storage pods. So we should try to avoid local persistent volumes on GPU nodes where possible.
maya: Agreed. We'll inventory local-storage usage and move checkpoint data to shared FS (NFS/S3 FUSE) where it makes sense.
ash: Quick command to see blocking pods on a node: `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-45 -o go-template='{{range .items}}{{.metadata.namespace}}/{{.metadata.name}}: safeToEvict='{{index .metadata.annotations "cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict"}}'`

lee: Also add a monitoring alert: `gpu-nodepool-scale-blocked` that fires when CA reports repeated `not evictable` events > 3 in 30m.
maya: I'll start with the audit and a small PoC controller to toggle the annotation during nightly scale window. Will update here. Thanks. :thumbsup:
ash: Thanks — happy to help with the controller RBAC and testing on staging.
infra-bot: [note] recorded action: maya started a runbook PR: /infra/gpu-scale-safe-evict in repo infraops (link)
